subject: CS+Eng sync: model shortlist & context window decision
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Zhang <amelia@holodoc.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CS+Eng sync: model shortlist & context window decision

Hi Amelia —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Per our call I pulled together a short working list of candidate models and a quick summary of context/window options. I attached the CSV with the shortlist and a short PDF that shows how we handle prefix caching, fallback routing, and large-window routing in the platform.

Two quick asks to lock down the implementation plan:
- Can you confirm typical note size (avg tokens per clinical note) and the fraction of requests that need the full 32k window vs the shorter 8k window? The attached estimate you sent earlier looked like ~1.2k tokens avg but I want to make sure we account for the OCR+metadata case.
- Do you have a target p90 latency and a budgeted cost-per-1000-requests in mind for the pilot? Those will drive the default model and routing choices.

Proposed next steps (we can run the pilot once we align):
1) Lock shortlist and default windowing (8k default, allow 32k for batch/exports)
2) Pilot traffic (2 weeks, 10k user sessions/day simulated)
3) Evaluate quality/cost and switch to hybrid routing if needed

Attachments: holodoc_model_shortlist_v1.csv, context_walkthrough_v2.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if it helps.

—Kimberly Park
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference

From: Amelia Zhang <amelia@holodoc.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@holodoc.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CS+Eng sync: model shortlist & context window decision

Thanks Kimberly —

Confirming details from our side:
- Average clinical note after OCR and redaction is ~1,350 tokens. Rough distribution: 65% under 2k, 25% between 2k–8k, ~10% above 8k. The >8k cases are mostly batch export jobs or long radiology reports.
- For the pilot, aim for p90 <= 750ms for interactive flows. Cost target: roughly $0.50–$0.80 per 1k interactive requests (we know pilot numbers are noisy). For batch exports we are comfortable with slower response times.

I attached the usage estimate spreadsheet we compiled (holodoc_api_usage_estimate.xlsx) — it includes monthly active user numbers and a rough QPS profile (peak 120 QPS, sustained 20 QPS).

One operational note: HoloDoc requires that PHI content is isolated; our security team prefers a private deployment for production, but pilot can run on Redwood Hosted if we sign an addendum restricting retention. We can confirm legal next week.

Happy to review the shortlist — can you call out which models you expect to be our default vs fallback?

—Amelia
Product Ops, HoloDoc
amelia@holodoc.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Zhang <amelia@holodoc.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CS+Eng sync: model shortlist & context window decision

Looping in a couple of quick CS operational thoughts from my side:

- Candidate shortlist (initial):
  * redwood-instruct-v2-13b (8k) — strong cost/latency balance for interactive Q&A
  * mistral-7b-instruct-8k (fast, cheap for short prompts)
  * llama-70b-32k-distilled (for long-window exports / summarization)

- Recommended default pattern: route interactive user queries to redwood-instruct-v2-13b with prefix caching for repeated patient-context. If token count > 8k, transparently promote to the 32k model for export workflows (batch or explicit user request).

Engineering questions I want answered before pilot:
1) Do we permit dynamic model swaps per-request (yes if latency trade is acceptable) or do we prefer session-level pinning?
2) Is the 750ms p90 strict for the whole stack, or only the model inference time? That affects batching decisions.
3) Are there any region constraints — do we need EU-hosted inference nodes for certain clinics?

Related links: HubSpot deal HL-2026-0783, Drive folder with data sample.

I can take point on quality checks during the pilot — I'll prepare 25 prompt variants (short/long/edge cases) to run daily.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Amelia Zhang <amelia@holodoc.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CS+Eng sync: model shortlist & context window decision

Thanks — quick engineering alignment from my side.

Plan proposal:
- Pilot default model: redwood-instruct-v2-13b (8k). Fallback: llama-70b-32k-distilled for ops requiring large windows.
- Routing: request-level dynamic routing (we'll enable session pinning as an opt-in if Amelia's team wants consistent per-session latency).
- Latency: we'll target model inference p90 <= 650ms for the 13b path (leaving headroom for network + app to meet your 750ms p90).
- Cost controls: enable prefix caching for repeated patient context, continuous batching tuned to keep p90 under 750ms at 20 QPS sustained. For peak spikes we'll rely on autoscale + a temporary increased burst cap.
- Security/Deployment: pilot on Hosted with a retention addendum; production should be Private (VPC) given PHI requirement — I'll flag infra for a Private onboarding.

Timeline:
- Week of 10/5: start pilot (synthetic traffic + small subset of live users)
- 10/19: evaluate pilot metrics (latency, cost, quality); Marissa will share daily prompt check results
- 10/26: decision for rollout cadence (expand vs iterate)

I've attached a small pilot metrics template (pilot-metrics-template.csv). Marissa/Vivek to own instrumentation; Kimberly to coordinate HoloDoc confirmations.

If that looks good Amelia, we'll schedule a 30m kickoff for Mon 10/5 to confirm test users and retention terms.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
